title: monthsToTriage starts from every priced line of every accepted re-run, a scan of the practice's priced history on every mapping view
evidence: mapped-plan.ts:428-434: `candidate` = every priced_line with unpriced_reason IS NULL in any accepted re-run in effect (`accepted`). Each candidate then goes through PRICED_IN_EFFECT, a per-line EXISTS and priced_line_shortfall_cents(p.id). This query runs on every mapping list and every plan page view. Failing sequence: a practice accepts re-runs after a release or a sign-off (common). Those re-runs hold almost all of its priced lines, so each page view scans its whole priced history. That is the full-scan pattern #81 removed and that MAPPED_NOT_PRICED (mapped-plan.ts:179-185) avoids by starting from priced_line_by_reason. The result is unchanged because the EXISTS at :439 already requires an earlier NO_MAPPING row for the line, so restricting the candidates first costs nothing in accuracy.
fix: Build `candidate` from lines that some eligible run left NO_MAPPING: `SELECT DISTINCT x.service_line_id FROM pricing_run r JOIN priced_line x ON x.pricing_run_id = r.id AND x.unpriced_reason = 'NO_MAPPING' WHERE r.practice_id = $1 AND ELIGIBLE_RUN('r')`, which uses priced_line_by_reason. Keep the outer conditions as they are. Add a db test that runs an accepted re-run with many priced lines and checks the plan (or the row count of the candidate CTE).

verdict.reason:
F1 holds, but its proposed fix needs one correction.

Evidence checked at 8517ee3a:
- In mapped-plan.ts:427-434, `candidate` is every priced_line with unpriced_reason IS NULL from accepted re-runs in effect. That set goes into PRICED_IN_EFFECT (apps/worker/src/price/in-effect.ts:39-43). Each row it returns then runs the EXISTS at :437-439, priced_line_shortfall_cents, the case_line NOT EXISTS and the line_status subquery.
- The planner cannot move the EXISTS ahead of in_effect. The EXISTS uses a.created_at, and in_effect is a DISTINCT ON.
- monthsToTriage runs on every mapping list and plan page view (apps/web/src/lib/routes/mapping.ts:100).
- MAPPED_NOT_PRICED (:180-184) starts from NO_MAPPING rows through priced_line_by_reason, as F1 says.

Reproduction: I built a scratch database on 5433 with the same priced_line indexes, then dropped it. It held 24 months of 10,000 lines each, with a first run and an accepted re-run per month, and 20 NO_MAPPING lines. The current `candidate` returns 240,000 rows, so the whole history of those months goes through DISTINCT ON and the per-row checks on every page view. The proposed `candidate` returns 20 rows from an index scan on priced_line_by_reason in 0.3 ms.

Problem with the fix: F1 says restricting the candidates "costs nothing in accuracy", but the fix as written does change results. The EXISTS at :437-439 accepts a NO_MAPPING row from ANY earlier run, not only an eligible one. Design §4.2 (line 294) says "Any earlier pricing counts". The proposed `candidate` adds ELIGIBLE_RUN('r'), which drops complete-but-unaccepted re-runs and failed runs. A line whose only earlier NO_MAPPING row is in such a run would no longer be listed. Example: unaccepted re-run R1 left the line NO_MAPPING, then accepted re-run R2 priced it with a shortfall. This needs a run that left a line NO_MAPPING after an eligible run had priced it, which is an edge case. Even so, the fix should copy the EXISTS's run condition exactly so the two queries give the same result.

Severity: should-fix. This costs server time on frequently viewed pages but changes no number.
verdict.fix:
In monthsToTriage (mapped-plan.ts:430-432), replace `candidate` with
`SELECT DISTINCT x.service_line_id FROM pricing_run r JOIN priced_line x ON x.pricing_run_id = r.id AND x.unpriced_reason = 'NO_MAPPING' WHERE r.practice_id = $1`.
Leave out ELIGIBLE_RUN so the candidate set uses the same run condition as the EXISTS at :437-439, which accepts any earlier run. The query still uses priced_line_by_reason. Keep the outer conditions, including the EXISTS with q.created_at < a.created_at. In the comment, say that the candidates are the lines any run left NO_MAPPING, read through priced_line_by_reason (#81).

Add db tests in mapped-plan.db.test.ts:
1. An accepted re-run with many priced lines that were never NO_MAPPING. It is not listed, and an EXPLAIN or a row count shows `candidate` holds only the NO_MAPPING lines.
2. A line whose only earlier NO_MAPPING pricing is in an unaccepted re-run, later priced with a shortfall by an accepted re-run. It is still listed, which keeps the current behaviour.

title: Audit report's unmapped-plan line count is untested; the plan count in its place passes every test
evidence: Mutation M18 changed content.ts:1077 `lines: coverage.unmapped_plans.reduce((total, plan) => total + plan.lines, 0)` to `lines: coverage.unmapped_plans.length`. All db tests in apps/worker/src/report, report-documents-routes.db.test.ts and audit-e2e.db.test.ts still pass (70/70), as do the mapped-plan, mapping-routes, price and monitor db tests (90/90) and the unit tests (121/121). The streamed.db.test whole-read equivalence check (test-support/whole-read.ts:780-782) uses a world with no NO_MAPPING lines, and report.test.ts:185-190 only tests unmappedPlansText on hand-built input. Failing input: a run with one unmapped plan holding 3 lines. The stored audit report would say '1 plan had no mapping when this run was priced; its lines are not priced (1 line, ...)' instead of 3 lines, so the report's sentence would no longer match stored coverage.
fix: Add a db test (streamed.db.test or audit-e2e) where the run holds an unmapped plan with more than one line. Check content.coverage.unmapped_plans against Coverage's tp-pricing-coverage/2 counts and integer cents. Also check that the whole-read and streamed outputs agree in that world.

verdict.reason:
F8 holds. At 8517ee3a, content.ts:1075-1079 builds the stored audit report's coverage.unmapped_plans as follows: plans is the length of the run coverage's unmapped_plans, lines is the sum of each plan's lines, and charge_cents is the sum of each plan's charge_cents. I searched every *.test.ts and *.test.tsx file in the repo. No test reads coverage.unmapped_plans from audit content that the code actually built.
- report.test.ts:178-190 and test-support/audit-content.ts:114 both use hand-built content.
- streamed.db.test and audit-e2e.db.test have no NO_MAPPING lines.
- report-documents-routes.db.test.ts:231 checks the coverage report's readiness, which is about plans waiting now. It does not check the audit report's run coverage.
- price.db.test and mapping-routes.db.test check the run's stored coverage, not the report built from it.
- whole-read.ts:780-783 is an exact copy of the same expression. So the whole-read equivalence check could only catch a change made to one side, and only in a world that has unmapped lines, which no test builds.

Mutation M18 (lines becomes the plan count) therefore survives. So would changes to the plans count or the charge_cents sum. The failing input is a run with one unmapped plan holding 3 lines: the stored, immutable report would say "1 line" while the run's coverage records 3. I did not rerun the mutation, because the search covers every test and the evidence is accurate.

Should-fix is the right grade. This is a dollar-and-count figure in a stored, immutable report, and under rules 1 and 3 the code that computes it must be tested. But the code as written is correct, so it does not block. The proposed fix is right but should go further (see fix).
verdict.fix: Add a db test in streamed.db.test or audit-e2e.db.test. Price a run that holds at least two unmapped plans, one with 3 or more lines and one that includes a negative-charge line. Check that the built content.coverage.unmapped_plans has plans equal to the length of the run coverage's unmapped_plans, lines equal to the sum of their lines, and charge_cents equal to the sum of their charge_cents as integer-cents text. Check the rendered unmappedPlansText sentence too. Run the whole-read and streamed builds in that world and check that they agree. That test fails under M18 and under the matching mutations to plans and charge_cents.

title: D2b's condition in monthsToQueue (queue only when the mapping completes a month holding this plan) is untested
evidence: Mutation M6 replaced `complete.some((month) => month.planIds.includes(planId))` at mapped-plan.ts:149 with `complete.length > 0`. No db or unit test fails. Failing sequence: month M1 is complete but not yet priced, e.g. its location hold has just been released (held changes from 'location' to null). A person then maps plan C, whose only month M2 is still mixed. With the mutation, mapping C queues a monitor job for M1, which design D2b says must not happen (the daily monitor plans that month). The current code is right, but nothing guards it.
fix: Add a monthsToQueue unit case (and a mapping-routes db case) where a complete month does not hold planId and the mapping completes no month: expect [] and no monitor job queued.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds. I did not run the mutant. I checked every test by hand against the mutated condition.

- **Evidence matches the code.** At 8517ee3a, apps/web/src/lib/pricing/mapped-plan.ts:149 is the D2b gate, `if (!complete.some((month) => month.planIds.includes(planId))) return [];`.
- **No test case has the state that would catch the mutant.** I traced every `monthsToQueue` assertion (mapped-plan.db.test.ts:153, 157, 165, 169, 183 and 450) and every monitor-job assertion in mapping-routes.db.test.ts (273-283, 291-338, 385-419, 421-433, 435-445) with `complete.length > 0` in place of the gate. Each case either has no complete month (no mapping yet, A mapped and both months mixed, location held, no release in force), or every complete month holds the plan just mapped.
  - In mapped-plan.db.test.ts, February holds b when b is mapped, and March holds c when c is mapped.
  - In the route test, February is priced before C is mapped.
  - In the D22 race test, the person whose mapping completes the month is the one who maps its last plan.
  - No case has a complete, unheld, uncovered month that does not hold the plan while the mapping completes nothing, so the mutant survives. There is no unit test file for mapped-plan.ts.
- **A more realistic failing sequence exists than the finding's.** The finding uses a location hold that has just been released, but the location save queues the monitor itself (settings.ts:712-720), so that window is short. Better: month M1 has all plans mapped and is held on content. A person maps plan C, whose only month M2 stays mixed. A mapping is a terms change (termsUnchangedSince), so M1 now reads terms_changed, its hold drops to null and it counts as complete. The current code returns [], as design §4.1 item 2 requires ("at least one month holds this plan's lines"). The mutant queues a monitor job for M1.
- **Severity:** what ships today is correct, so this is only a missing test. It stays should-fix rather than a nit because a design decision (D2b) has no guard and the mutant survives.
- **The fix is right.** A pure unit case is the cheapest and most direct guard. The mapping-routes db case is optional.
verdict.fix:
Add apps/web/src/lib/pricing/mapped-plan.test.ts with synthetic MonthAwaitingMappings and no database. It needs two cases:
(1) M1 is complete with planIds [A, B] and held null. M2 is mixed with planIds [A, C] and unmappedPlanIds [B2], so mapping C completes nothing. Then monthsToQueue(months, C) must equal [].
(2) A positive D20 case: a mapping that completes a month holding the plan lists every complete month, oldest first, including ones that do not hold the plan, capped at MONITOR_MONTHS_LIMIT.
Optionally add a mapping-routes db case: a month held on content with all its plans mapped, then a mapping of a plan found only in a mixed month. Expect the notice to be mapped and no monitor job queued.

title: The location-wait reopen on a new release in force is untested
evidence: Mutation M10 dropped `|| inForce !== row.failed_release_no` from the location_not_ready branch at mapped-plan.ts:383. No test fails. Failing sequence: a re-run fails location_not_ready under release N, and release N+1 comes into force with no location saved since. The correct code shows the month 'ready'. The mutant leaves it 'rerun_failed' (wait: location), so 'Price these months again' stays withheld after the new release.
fix: In mapped-plan.db.test.ts, add a case with a failed location_not_ready re-run, a new release in force and no location saved: expect kind 'ready' with lastFailure.reason 'location'.

verdict.reason:
F5 holds: the code path is real and nothing tests it. At 8517ee3a, apps/web/src/lib/pricing/mapped-plan.ts:383 reads `const open = row.location_saved_since === true || inForce !== row.failed_release_no;`. Design rev 3 line 282 says the location wait opens on either of two things: a location save after the re-run was created, or a release in force that differs from the re-run's. The design's test plan (line 569) lists only the save case.

stateOf is not exported, and toPriceAgain is called only from apps/web/src/lib/pricing/mapped-plan.db.test.ts. The location_not_ready cases there and elsewhere all keep the same release in force:
- :175 tests the awaiting list's `held` flag, not stateOf.
- :357-374 covers only the save path.
- mapping-routes.db.test.ts:485 marks a re-run failed and asserts 'rerun_failed', with no release change.

So deleting `|| inForce !== row.failed_release_no` (mutation M10) changes no tested result. The failing sequence is accurate: release N+1 comes into force after a location_not_ready re-run under N, with no save since. The correct code reads 'ready' with reason 'location'; the mutant keeps 'rerun_failed' and withholds "Price these months again". I confirmed this by reading the code and tests; I did not run the mutation.

Severity stays at nit. A regression would hide the button (it fails safe): no dollar amount, stage or approval goes wrong, and the daily monitor does not depend on this state.

The proposed fix is right and cheap. The test file already switches releases (w.withdraw; 900004 put in force and rolled back near :344; loadContentGapRelease making 900007 in force at :434).

A related gap the test should also pin down: with no release in force, `inForce` is null, and `null !== N` makes the location branch read 'ready'. The content branch guards `inForce !== null` and reads 'rerun_failed'. That mismatch is cosmetic, because a press is refused anyway while no release is in force.
verdict.fix:
In mapped-plan.db.test.ts, extend the 'reads rerun_failed for a re-run that stopped on the billing ZIP' case (around :357-374), or add a new case:
1. Create the failed location_not_ready re-run under RERUN_RELEASE (or the base release), without calling setLocation.
2. Put another release in force (the existing helpers already do this, e.g. 900004 or w.loadContentGapRelease).
3. Expect `(await toPriceAgain(practice))[0]?.state` to equal `{ kind: 'ready', lastFailure: { rerunId, failureCode: 'location_not_ready', reason: 'location' } }`, and expect priceAgainSets(...).ready to include the month.

Also assert the no-release-in-force case. Best is to make it agree with the content branch by changing line 383 to `inForce !== null && inForce !== row.failed_release_no` (rerun_failed while nothing is in force), then pin that in the test.

title: MAPPED_NOT_PRICED's use of the mapping in force on the line's date is untested
evidence: Mutation M19 replaced the join on `payer_plan_mapping_in_force(l.payer_plan_key, coalesce(l.service_date, c.service_from))` with the plan's newest mapping regardless of date (a LATERAL ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1). No test fails. Failing sequence: plan P is mapped effective_from 2026-09-01, and an August line of P was correctly priced NO_MAPPING. With the mutant, August is listed as 'mapped, not priced', counted in Figure 2 (PRC-31) and offered under 'Price these months again'. Re-pricing it would leave it NO_MAPPING again, so it would be offered forever.
fix: Add a db case with a mapping whose effective_from is after a NO_MAPPING line's service date. Expect the line absent from mappedNotPricedTotals and from monthsToPriceAgain.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds. In apps/web/src/lib/pricing/mapped-plan.ts:189, MAPPED_NOT_PRICED joins on payer_plan_mapping_in_force(l.payer_plan_key, coalesce(l.service_date, c.service_from)). Three test files reach this query: apps/web/src/lib/pricing/mapped-plan.db.test.ts, apps/web/src/lib/routes/mapping-routes.db.test.ts and apps/web/e2e/mapping.spec.ts. In all three, every mapping starts on 2026-01-01: mapFixed at mapped-plan.db.test.ts:96, w.mapped at :190 and :362, pricing-world.ts:69 and :123, and mapAs at mapping-routes.db.test.ts:255. No fixture sets an end date (effective_to) or a superseding mapping, and every line falls in February, March or October 2026. So for every fixture, the mapping in force on the line's date is also the plan's newest mapping. A mutant that joins the newest mapping by created_at (M19) gives the same rows, and no test can fail.

The failure can happen in practice. If plan P is mapped from 2026-09-01, an August line stays NO_MAPPING after pricing, which is correct. The mutant would still count that line in Figure 2 (PRC-31) and offer August under 'Price these months again'. A re-run uses the date-based lookup, so it would leave the line NO_MAPPING again. The function's other two behaviours are also untested through this query: it returns NULL when two mappings overlap on a date, and it follows the supersedes_id chain.

I checked this by reading the code and fixtures. I did not build a writable worktree or run the mutant, but every fixture in the three files was checked, so the static evidence covers them all. The proposed fix is right but narrower than it should be.

I raised the severity from nit to should-fix. The gap guards a figure users see and a re-pricing offer. Plans mapped for only some dates are a real case: the product already names them in its Coverage text.
verdict.fix: In mapped-plan.db.test.ts, add a case where one run holds lines on both sides of a mapping's start date. Load the February run with plan B unmapped, then map B from 2026-02-15 (use w.mapped or a variant of mapFixed that takes a date). Expect mappedNotPricedTotals to count only B's lines dated on or after Feb 15, with their exact lines and cents, and expect the run listed in monthsToPriceAgain. Add a second case where B is mapped from 2026-03-01: expect zero lines in the figure and February absent from monthsToPriceAgain, for the practice and on B's page. Together these kill M19 and the opposite mutant that drops lines when a plan is mapped for only part of the month. Optionally add a superseding correction so the supersedes_id chain is also tested through this query.

title: monthsToTriage's rule that the NO_MAPPING row came from an earlier run is untested
evidence: Mutation M8 removed `AND q.created_at < a.created_at` from the EXISTS at mapped-plan.ts:439. No test fails. Failing sequence: a line priced in an accepted re-run, then left NO_MAPPING by a later run that is not in effect (e.g. a pending or failed re-run after a mapping correction). With the mutant, that line counts as 'newly priced by mapping' and appears in the months-to-triage offer.
fix: Add a db case where the only NO_MAPPING row for a line comes from a run created after the accepted re-run in effect. Expect monthsToTriage to omit it.

verdict.reason:
F4 does not hold. The claim that no test covers it is accurate: no test makes a NO_MAPPING row in a run created after the accepted re-run, so mutant M8 survives. But the failing sequence cannot happen through the application, so M8 is an equivalent mutant and does not point to a gap a test could catch.

I tried to reproduce it with a scratch db test in a detached worktree at 8517ee3a, against PostgreSQL 18 on port 5433:
1. Map plans A and B from 2026-01-01, run February, sign off a contract version, then re-run and accept.
2. Call correctMapping on B, superseding its mapping with one effective from 2026-03-01.
3. Re-run the accepted run and execute it, leaving it pending.

The later run priced all 7 lines and left none NO_MAPPING, both on the original code and on the mutant.

Why it can't happen:
- payer_plan_mapping only takes inserts. Its rules trigger rejects UPDATE, and tp_app is granted INSERT only, with no DELETE (20261016160000_contracts_and_mapping.sql:676).
- payer_plan_mapping_in_force (packages/db/functions/payer_plan_mapping_in_force.sql) drops a mapping only when a correction that itself covers the date supersedes it.
- The overlap check in payer_plan_mapping_rules lets a new mapping overlap only the mappings it supersedes, directly or through a chain.

So once a plan is mapped on a date, it stays mapped. A run executed after the accepted re-run A can leave a line NO_MAPPING only if the plan was unmapped at every earlier execution. A re-run prices its original's lines (same cut-off), and the original executed before A was created. So any later NO_MAPPING row for a line in A comes with an earlier one, from a run created before A. Removing `AND q.created_at < a.created_at` changes no result the app can produce. The db case F4 proposes can only be built from priced_line rows written by a superuser, not through the app.

Notes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/aa4b05fd-cf7b-57fe-8086-b5b14b24e00e/scratchpad/progress/verify-payment-engine-F4.md.
verdict.fix: No test needed. Keep the clause: design §294 specifies it and it is a guard in depth. Optionally add a comment at mapped-plan.ts:439 saying the clause has no effect today because a mapped plan date never becomes unmapped (mappings are insert-only and only a correction that covers the date supersedes one). Record M8 as an equivalent mutant in the mutation report.

verdict.reason: The finding holds. At 8517ee3a, monthMixed (apps/web/src/lib/pricing/mapped-plan.ts:139) is called only from monthsWaitingForMappings (:163), and that is called only from routes/mapping.ts:97. The only tests that call monthsWaitingForMappings are in mapped-plan.db.test.ts:158-166, and every month there has held=null. title: NOTHING_MAPPED says a month is priced once every plan it holds is mapped; in fact it is priced once any plan is
evidence: routes/pricing.ts:411: '...and each month is priced once every plan it holds is mapped'. Under ADR 0075, the daily and document monitor, 'Price them now' and this form all price a month as soon as any one of its plans is mapped, with the unmapped plans' lines left NO_MAPPING. The design's mixed-month handling and the monitor tests confirm this. The person is told to wait for every plan when mapping one is enough.
fix: Reword it, e.g. 'none of the period's plans has a mapping yet, so a run would price nothing: map them on Payer and plan mapping; each month is priced once any plan it holds is mapped, and the rest once theirs are.' Update the design's §2.2 text to match.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds. At 8517ee3a, pricing.ts:410-411 tells the person that "each month is priced once every plan it holds is mapped". The code disagrees in three places. createPricingRun (create.ts:127-129) refuses only when every plan of the period is unmapped (unmapped.length === plans.length), so one mapped plan is enough for a run. The daily monitor (monitor/plan.ts:313-336) creates runs for months that hold both mapped and unmapped plans. And create.ts's own comment (create.ts:55-58) and PRD.md:175 say a month is priced "once a mapping completes it, or by the daily monitoring once any of its plans is mapped".

Failing sequence: month M holds plans A and B, neither mapped, and the person submits the form and gets this error. They then map A. The message says M still waits for B. In fact, resubmitting the same form now creates a run that leaves B's lines NO_MAPPING, and the daily monitor prices M within a day anyway.

The message is half true. Under the design's D2b rule, mapping a plan queues pricing at once only when it completes a month, so it is right about that path and leaves out the other two.

I tried to refute it as a deliberate nudge to map every plan first, but the sentence states a fact rather than giving advice. The test at pricing-routes.db.test.ts:226 checks only the start of the message, so rewording the end breaks no test.

The proposed fix is itself inaccurate. "The rest once theirs are" implies the other plans' lines get priced automatically. They do not: they need "Price these months again" and acceptance by hand (design §4). The proposed wording also drops the D2b advice that mapping every plan first avoids re-runs.

The finding names only the design, but the same wrong text is also in ADR 0075:78-80.

The grade stays nit: this is user-facing wording only. No amount, stage or data is affected, and the daily monitor limits any wait to a day.
verdict.fix: Replace NOTHING_MAPPED (apps/web/src/lib/routes/pricing.ts:411) with: "none of the period’s plans has a mapping yet, so a run would price nothing: map them on Payer and plan mapping. A month is priced as soon as every plan it holds is mapped, or once any one is, by the daily monitoring or a run from here; its other plans’ lines then need it priced again." Make the same change in ADR 0075:78-80 and design §2.2 (line 112). The test at pricing-routes.db.test.ts:226 checks only the start of the message, so it needs no change.

title: A re-run counts only if created after the newest mapping, though it reads mappings when it prices: a queued re-run that will price the new plan reads 'ready' and a second re-run is offered
evidence: mapped-plan.ts:326 counts a re-run only when q.created_at > k.newest_mapping_at. execute.ts reads loadAgreementRecords inside the pricing transaction, when the re-run prices, not when it was created. Sequence (scratch test zz-scratch-r2.db.test.ts, passing): February holds plans A, B and C. Map A, then price the first run (B and C left NO_MAPPING). Map B, then createRerun RR (queued). Map C, then execute RR. RR is complete with 14 lines, 0 of them NO_MAPPING, and RERUN_ACCEPTANCE 'awaiting'. Yet monthsToPriceAgain returns [{kind:'ready', lastFailure:null}] and priceAgainSets(...).ready has 1 run. The page hides RR's 'Priced again: review and accept' link and offers 'Price these months again (1)'. Pressing creates RR2, an identical re-run of the same month, which then supersedes or competes with RR for a hand acceptance. That breaks MAP-08's 'one counting re-run per month' and D4. mapped-plan.db.test.ts:286-308 pins the wrong state: afterB is still queued, so it will read C's mapping, but the test expects 'ready'.
fix: Count a re-run from what it read, not when it was created. (a) Any re-run still 'queued' counts, since it reads current mappings when it prices. (b) A complete re-run counts when it holds none of the run's listed service lines as NO_MAPPING (join its priced_line on those service_line_ids, through priced_line_once). (c) Only a 'running' re-run falls back to the created_at rule. title: Any mapping counts as 'mapped', even one not in force on the line's service date: the user is told the month is being priced, and a run prices nothing
evidence: Three places test only that some mapping exists, never its effective dates: monthsAwaitingMappings at mapped-plan.ts:101, unmappedPlanTotals in mapping-queries.ts (its NOT EXISTS has no date predicate), and createPricingRun's MAP-07 guard at create.ts:127 (practiceUnmappedPlanIds in contracts/load.ts:260, a set of plan IDs). Coverage's waiting figure (UNCOVERED, mapping-queries.ts:20) does check dates. Reproduced: MAP-06's February 2026 file; both plans mapped no_agreement effective 2026-06-01. Result: redirect ?notice=mapped_pricing; a monitor job with months ['2026-02-01']; the monitor creates a complete run with 0 lines priced and 7 NO_MAPPING. The run's planned 'nothing mapped' refusal (MAP-07) is bypassed. unmappedPlans is {plans:0} and mappedNotPriced is {lines:0}, so the dashboard, Pricing runs and the report readiness say every plan is mapped while none of the month's lines can price. Price-again also never offers the month. Design line 68 chose 'no mapping at all' on purpose, but that choice produces a false notice and a run that prices nothing, which fails the accuracy test of the founder's standing rule.
fix: Treat a plan as mapped for a month only when a mapping covers each line's service date. Use UNCOVERED's predicate (m.effective_from <= service date AND (effective_to IS NULL OR service date < effective_to)) in monthsAwaitingMappings and unmappedPlanTotals, and make the createPricingRun guard refuse when no line of the period has a mapping in force. Add MAP-07/MAP-01 cases for a mapping whose dates exclude the month.

verdict.reason:
The finding is real only in a narrow form, and several of its claims don't hold. I did not reproduce it in the database; the code path below is direct.

What holds:
- `monthsAwaitingMappings` (apps/web/src/lib/pricing/mapped-plan.ts:101) checks only that some mapping exists. It never checks the mapping's dates.
- The same is true of `unmappedPlanTotals` (apps/web/src/lib/contracts/mapping-queries.ts:559) and of the `createPricingRun` guard (apps/worker/src/price/create.ts:127-130). That guard goes through `practiceUnmappedPlanIds`, which uses the date-blind `unmappedPlanIds`.
- So a month whose plans are all mapped, but none on the month's dates, counts as complete under `monthComplete`. Mapping its last plan queues a monitor job at once and shows the `mapped_pricing` notice. The first run then prices no lines; every line is NO_MAPPING.
- That month is now covered by a run. When a mapping that does cover its dates arrives later, the month no longer gets a first run on completion. It needs "Price these months again" and someone accepting the re-run. That works against the D2b onboarding goal (first runs, no re-run, no hand acceptance), so it is a small accuracy and time-to-value gap in the new completion trigger.

What does not hold:
1. Not introduced by this PR. At base 83d71fd6, `assertPricingAllowed` and `pricingReadiness` also used "no mapping at all". The base daily monitor would create the same run that prices nothing within a day. So "MAP-07 bypassed" and "a run prices nothing" describe existing behaviour, which design rule 2 and MAP-02 chose on purpose. The PR only makes it happen sooner and adds the notice.
2. The screens are not misleading:
   - Coverage shows `EveryPlanMappedAlert`, which says lines outside every mapping's dates stay unpriced as NO_MAPPING. That matches base's "Pricing can run" text.
   - Coverage's waiting card, the home page's `plansWaiting` (`dollarsWaitingOnMapping`) and the coverage report's `waiting` and `waiting_plans` all use the date-aware UNCOVERED rule, so they show these lines.
   - `unmappedPlans` is defined and labelled as "no mapping at all", and it is accurate by that definition.
3. The notice is not false: a run is created. "Price again" correctly offers nothing until a mapping is in force on those dates.

On the proposed fix: making the creation guard check dates changes MAP-02 and design rule 2 (a separate decision). It would also need new wording, because plan pages would show those plans as mapped. The narrower and better fix is to make the completion test (`monthsAwaitingMappings`) date-aware, so a mapping only queues pricing for months it actually covers. Notes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/aa4b05fd-cf7b-57fe-8086-b5b14b24e00e/scratchpad/progress/verify-security-F2.md.
verdict.fix: In `monthsAwaitingMappings` (mapped-plan.ts:101), count a plan as mapped for a month only when a mapping is in force on its lines' dates. Use UNCOVERED's predicate on `coalesce(l.service_date, c.service_from)`: `m.effective_from <= d AND (m.effective_to IS NULL OR d < m.effective_to)`. Then a mapping whose dates exclude the month neither queues monitoring nor shows `mapped_pricing`, and the month gets its first run when a mapping that covers it arrives. Leave `unmappedPlanTotals` and the `createPricingRun` guard as they are ("no mapping at all", as at base and as design rule 2 and MAP-02 intend). Changing them would be a separate design decision. title: price_waiting is permission-checked in the handler only, not in Postgres
evidence: priceWaitingAction (mapping.ts:319-323) writes no row to Postgres apart from the route's audit event. Its only other effect is an afterCommit enqueue of 'monitor', so the database never checks that the actor holds mapping.edit (CLAUDE.md: check in the handler and in Postgres). The handler's permission check and the worker's suspension gate do apply. The monitor creates runs in the job's own name, so the database never attributes those runs to the person or checks their permission for them. The settings route's monitor enqueue (settings.ts:720) follows a database write that Postgres checks.
fix: Record the request through a SECURITY DEFINER function or an insert under a policy that checks the actor's mapping.edit permission, so a handler-only bypass cannot queue monitoring.

verdict.reason:
The facts in the finding are right, but they do not make a defect. At 8517ee3a, priceWaitingAction (apps/web/src/lib/routes/mapping.ts:310-325) checks mapping.edit in the handler. It then only runs requirePlan's SELECT and an afterCommit enqueue of a request-keyed 'monitor' job.

1. Postgres does check this request in part. The route's audit insert goes through the audit_event_record policy (packages/db/migrations/20261015180000_tenancy_hardening.sql:433-439). That policy requires actor_id = app_actor_id() and that the practice is in app.practice_ids. It checks that the actor belongs to the practice, though not that they hold mapping.edit.

2. Queuing the job gives the person no new power and changes no data in their name. A monitor job without months plans every month no run covers as first runs. That is exactly what the daily monitor does anyway (design §1 line 14, rule 3 line 70: "The daily monitor and 'Price them now' plan every month no run covers"). It creates no re-run and no acceptance. The worker gates the job on suspension again, and the request key queues it once. Bypassing the check gets nothing more than waiting for the daily run.

3. The same pattern is already in place. settings.ts:720 and console.ts:473 queue the same request-keyed monitor job. The CLAUDE.md rule about checking in the handler and in Postgres is about authorizing changes to data, and this route changes none.

4. The proposed fix would not do what it claims. The web app queues jobs through PgBossQueue on its own connection (apps/web/src/lib/uploads/queue.ts; services.ts:220 queueDatabaseUrl). Code that bypasses the handler could still call enqueue directly, whatever a SECURITY DEFINER function records. Real gating would need a new table of recorded requests and a check of that table in the worker, which adds complexity for no security gain.

So the finding is not real. At most it is an informational note.
verdict.fix: None needed. Optionally, the route's doc comment could say that the request needs no permission check in Postgres because the job does only what the daily monitor does.

title: The job-payload guard looks up `PAYLOAD_LISTS[key]` through the prototype chain, so keys like `constructor` or `toString` with a value of `[]` pass the guard
evidence: phi-guard.ts:155 `const list = PAYLOAD_LISTS[key]` on a plain object literal. For key 'constructor', 'toString', 'hasOwnProperty' or 'valueOf', `list` is the inherited function, not undefined. So `list.min` and `list.max` are undefined, both length comparisons are false, and `[].every(...)` is true: no finding, then `continue`. I confirmed it with a throwaway vitest file in packages/observability (since removed). jobPayloadPhiFindings({practice_id: <uuid>, constructor: []}) returned [], and so did {toString: []} and {hasOwnProperty: []}. By contrast, {foo: []} returned the expected two findings ('is not an ID field' and 'does not hold an opaque UUID'). This is a regression: at base 83d71fd6 the same keys reached `PAYLOAD_FIELDS[key]` (also inherited, but defined), and `typeof [] !== 'string'` raised 'is not in its fixed format'. A list of strings under such a key, e.g. {constructor: ['2026-02-01']}, now throws TypeError (`list.entry` is undefined) instead of returning a finding. The impact is limited: the admitted value is an empty array, which carries no data, and the guard runs only in tests (SEC-08), not at enqueue. Still, the guard no longer enforces its own rule that only *_id, period, day, words_version and months keys are allowed.
fix: Look up only own keys: `const list = Object.hasOwn(PAYLOAD_LISTS, key) ? PAYLOAD_LISTS[key] : undefined;` and the same for `PAYLOAD_FIELDS`. Alternatively, build both tables with `Object.freeze(Object.assign(Object.create(null), {...}))` or as a `Map`. Add `[{ constructor: [] }, /not an ID field/]` and `[{ toString: ['2026-02-01'] }, /not an ID field/]` to the refused cases in phi-guard.test.ts.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds, and I reproduced it at 8517ee3a. phi-guard.ts:143-145 builds PAYLOAD_LISTS as a plain object literal, and line 155 reads PAYLOAD_LISTS[key], which also finds members inherited from the object prototype. I ran a bundled copy of phi-guard.ts in node. {practice_id: uuid, constructor: []} returned [], and so did {toString: []}, while {foo: []} returned the expected two findings. {constructor: ['2026-02-01']} throws TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'test')". {constructor: 'x'} gets the wrong finding ('not in its fixed format' from the PAYLOAD_FIELDS lookup at :162), where it should be told the key is not allowed.

Two corrections to the evidence:
- Only the empty-array pass is a regression. At base 83d71fd6, a string value under 'constructor' already threw TypeError: PAYLOAD_FIELDS.constructor is the inherited Object function, and Object.test is undefined.
- Production is not affected. enqueue (apps/worker/src/jobs/enqueue.ts:18) checks every payload with the Zod parsePayload, so the gap is only in a test helper, and nit is the right grade.

The proposed fix is the right one. Plain-object tables used as lookups should never resolve inherited members.
verdict.fix: In jobPayloadPhiFindings, read both tables through own keys only. Use `const list = Object.hasOwn(PAYLOAD_LISTS, key) ? PAYLOAD_LISTS[key] : undefined;` and do the same for PAYLOAD_FIELDS at :162. Building both tables as frozen null-prototype objects or Maps also works. Add refused cases to phi-guard.test.ts: { constructor: [] }, { toString: ['2026-02-01'] } and { valueOf: 'x' }, each expecting /not an ID field/ and not a throw.
